rows.source: UKHSA pertussis prevention and public-health management
rows.verified: Pertussis is a bacterial chest infection that can cause prolonged, severe coughing fits.

rows.source: UKHSA pertussis prevention and public-health management
rows.verified: Pertussis is particularly dangerous for babies, especially those under 6 months old.

rows.source: UKHSA pertussis prevention and public-health management
rows.verified: Vaccination is the most effective way to protect against pertussis.

rows.source: UKHSA pertussis prevention and public-health management
rows.verified: Pertussis is notifiable in England and Wales, and clinical diagnosis may be notified without waiting for laboratory confirmation.

rows.source: UKHSA pertussis prevention and public-health management
rows.verified: Culture can confirm infection, while PCR and serological testing provide additional diagnostic methods.

rows.source: UKHSA pertussis prevention and public-health management
rows.verified: Antibiotics should be given promptly to eligible suspected, linked or confirmed cases to eradicate the organism and reduce ongoing transmission.

rows.source: UKHSA pertussis prevention and public-health management
rows.verified: Public-health action prioritises infants at high risk of severe disease and people likely to transmit infection to them.

rows.source: UKHSA pertussis prevention and public-health management
rows.verified: The national guidance covers case, contact and outbreak management in healthcare and educational settings and was updated in May 2026.

rows.source: UKHSA pertussis prevention and public-health management
rows.verified: Pertussis risk depends on vaccination, age, infectious stage, contact intensity, setting, testing, treatment timing and presence of vulnerable infants.

rows.source: UKHSA pertussis prevention and public-health management
rows.verified: UKHSA pertussis evidence is case-, contact-, vaccine-, setting-, outbreak- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level transmission probability.

rows.source: OPSS domestic upholstered-furniture fire safety
rows.verified: UK furniture fire-safety rules set flammability requirements for domestic upholstered furniture supplied in the United Kingdom.

rows.source: OPSS domestic upholstered-furniture fire safety
rows.verified: The Furniture and Furnishings Fire Safety Amendment Regulations 2025 came into force on 30 October 2025.

rows.source: OPSS domestic upholstered-furniture fire safety
rows.verified: The 2025 amendment removed specified baby and young-child products from the scope of the 1988 regulations.

rows.source: OPSS domestic upholstered-furniture fire safety
rows.verified: The 2025 amendment removed the requirement for manufacturers to attach a display label to new products.

rows.source: OPSS domestic upholstered-furniture fire safety
rows.verified: The 2025 amendment extended the period for starting legal proceedings from 6 months to 12 months.

rows.source: OPSS domestic upholstered-furniture fire safety
rows.verified: OPSS states that the existing regime has protected consumers for decades but requires modernisation to address innovation, compliance and chemical-flame-retardant concerns.

rows.source: OPSS domestic upholstered-furniture fire safety
rows.verified: The March 2026 consultation proposed future fire-safety requirements based on a smoulder test instead of mandatory open-flame testing.

rows.source: OPSS domestic upholstered-furniture fire safety
rows.verified: The 2026 proposals include options for component or composite testing and proportionate changes to product scope; these remain proposals pending final policy and legislation.

rows.source: OPSS domestic upholstered-furniture fire safety
rows.verified: Furniture fire risk depends on product type, upholstery and filling, ignition source, construction, test performance, condition, use, consumer behaviour and regulatory status.

rows.source: OPSS domestic upholstered-furniture fire safety
rows.verified: OPSS furniture evidence is product-, material-, test-, market-, regulatory- and time-specific and is not an exact parcel-level fire probability.
